title: Getting started
description: How a kiss-ssg site is laid out: starting one, the router.js build script, and the TypeScript types that ship with the package.

title: Converting an existing page
description: Turning a page you already have — a Claude or ChatGPT artifact, an exported page, a hand-written HTML file — into a structured kiss site that still looks the same.

title: Pages and data
description: Registering pages with .page() and .pages(), shaping their data with controllers, fetching remote models, and Markdown options.

title: Assets and builds
description: Copying and compiling assets, cache-busting URLs, running an external asset pipeline, cleaning the build folder, building several sites from one source, and how the dev watcher handles file changes.
sections: Building more than one site from one source tree

title: Sitemap, llms.txt and feeds
description: The files crawlers, feed readers and agents read, derived from the same page registry: sitemap.xml and robots.txt for search, an RSS feed, and llms.txt with a Markdown copy of every page for agents.

title: URLs and redirects
description: Telling kiss where the site is deployed and how its host serves URLs, keeping old addresses alive with redirect files, and letting the host cache hashed files for a year.

title: Learning packages
description: Zipping pages into IMS content packages and SCORM 1.2 packages for Moodle or any LMS: membership, what a package carries, two ways to build a lesson, and recording answers through the SCORM bridge.

title: Cookie consent
description: The consent manager built into kiss: services declared once in config.consent, the banner and settings, gated scripts and click-to-load embeds, Google Consent Mode, withdrawal, records of each choice, and what the audit checks.

title: Checking a build
description: Waiting for a build, dry-running it with kiss-ssg check, reading the report, recording a site's knowledge base with kiss-ssg aikb, and upgrading a site with kiss-ssg upgrade.

title: Helpers
description: The Handlebars helpers kiss-ssg registers for you, from link and asset to markdown, canonical and isActive, and how to add your own.
